h1:
Where to Stay in Bangkok?
12 Hotels We've Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites
heroSub: Twelve Bangkok hotels across every budget — 5-star luxury on the Chao Phraya River down to hostels from ฿300. Covering the areas travellers actually use: Riverside, Siam, Sukhumvit, Silom, Thonglor and Chinatown. Starting from around ฿300–16,000/night.
introH2: 🏙️ Why does choosing the right area in Bangkok matter so much?
introHtml: Bangkok traffic is a fact of life, so picking a hotel that's on the BTS/MRT or in the neighbourhood you actually want to explore matters even more than the hotel itself. Each area has a distinctly different feel — the Chao Phraya Riverside is quiet, luxurious and reached by boat · Siam is the shopping core right on the BTS · Sukhumvit is the food and nightlife strip along the skytrain · Silom is the business district on both BTS and MRT · Thonglor is the hip cafe and dining quarter · Chinatown is street food and old-town atmosphere. Many travellers book without checking the location, then spend the whole trip stuck in taxis at red lights. This guide brings together 12 Bangkok hotels we've reviewed across every tier — every pick comes from reading real guest reviews, with prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Bangkok has the BTS skytrain and MRT subway covering the main tourist areas, which avoids a lot of the traffic. From Suvarnabhumi Airport, take the Airport Rail Link and connect to BTS/MRT; from Don Muang, use taxi or bus. The main areas in this guide: Riverside — Mandarin Oriental, The Peninsula, reached by river ferry and hotel shuttle boats · Siam — Siam@Siam, ibis Siam, Lub d at BTS National Stadium, the shopping core · Sukhumvit — INNSiDE at BTS On Nut, The Salil near BTS Thong Lo · Silom — ibis Styles Silom, Silom Space near BTS Sala Daeng / MRT Silom · Chinatown — Shanghai Mansion, ASAI, Hotel Royal near MRT Wat Mangkon.

entries.name: Mandarin Oriental, Bangkok
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chao Phraya riverside·Bang Rak · hotel shuttle boat
entries.storyHtml: The highest score in this guide at 9.5 — the Mandarin Oriental is Thailand's oldest hotel, open since 1876, and the name people worldwide reach for when they think of riverside luxury in Bangkok. Real guest reviews praise the close, personal service that remembers your name, the riverside setting with a shuttle boat to the spa across the water, and the Authors' Wing that still carries the building's history. It suits a special-occasion trip where you want the very best of Bangkok.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: the entry-level Superior rooms face the city/garden — to get a river view you'll need to upgrade. Afternoon tea at the Authors' Lounge is famous; book ahead even if you're not staying.
pros: Thailand's oldest hotel, history stretching back to 1876
Legendary service — reviews praise the close, personal care
Chao Phraya riverside setting, charming boat access
Renowned restaurants and afternoon tea
cons: Highest price in this guide — best for a special-occasion trip
Entry-level rooms face the city/garden; river view costs more

entries.name: The Peninsula Bangkok
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chao Phraya riverside·Khlong San · hotel ferry
entries.addr: 333 Charoen Nakhon Road, Khlong San, Bangkok
entries.storyHtml: The Peninsula is a riverside luxury hotel on the Khlong San bank where every room faces the Chao Phraya, scoring 9.3 from over 1,099 reviews. What reviews mention most is the full river view from every room, the riverside pool, and the hotel ferry that crosses to the Saphan Taksin BTS connection. Being on the Thonburi side, it's quieter than the city-centre bank but still easy to reach town — ideal for a luxury stay where you want to wake up to the river.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: use the free hotel ferry to Saphan Taksin BTS — far easier than a car. Even the entry Deluxe rooms have a river view, so no need to upgrade to a suite if you're on a budget.
pros: Every room has a full Chao Phraya river view
Hotel ferry connects to Saphan Taksin BTS
Riverside pool and leafy gardens, restful setting
Over 1,099 reviews, consistent praise for views and service
cons: On the Thonburi side — you rely on the ferry or a car to cross
Pricey; better for a special trip than everyday sightseeing

entries.name: Siam@Siam Design Hotel Bangkok
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Siam · walk to BTS National Stadium
entries.addr: 865 Rama 1 Road, Wang Mai, Pathum Wan, Bangkok
entries.storyHtml: Siam@Siam has the best central-Siam location in this group and a hefty 1,299 reviews, scoring 9.2. The draw is its industrial-art design that turns reclaimed materials into artwork, plus a high-floor pool and Sky Bar with city views. Sitting opposite the National Stadium, it's a walk to BTS National Stadium, MBK and Siam Square — perfect if you want to shop and hop on the skytrain anywhere.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: ask for a high floor for the city view and quieter nights. A sunset drink at the Sky Bar is a highlight many reviews recommend.
pros: Central Siam — walk to BTS National Stadium, MBK, Siam Square
Distinctive industrial-art design, very photogenic
High-floor pool and Sky Bar with city views
1,299 reviews, consistent praise for location and design
cons: An older building — some corners show their age
Entry rooms are standard size; upgrade to a Studio for more space

entries.name: Shanghai Mansion Bangkok
entries.storyHtml: Shanghai Mansion is a 1930s-Shanghai-themed boutique hotel right on Yaowarat Road in the heart of Chinatown, scoring 9.2. The selling point is the all-in vintage Chinese decor — red lanterns, carved wood, and rooms named after Chinese flowers. It's slap in the middle of Yaowarat, so you step out to famous street food and can walk to MRT Wat Mangkon. Great for travellers who want to soak up Chinatown atmosphere and eat well all night.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: rooms sit above lively Yaowarat, which is busy all night — ask for an inner or high-floor room for quiet. Step out for street food in the evening with no taxi needed.
pros: Full 1930s Shanghai theme throughout — real atmosphere
Central Yaowarat location, famous street food at the door
Walk to MRT Wat Mangkon for easy access to town
High 9.2 score, praise for atmosphere and location
cons: Yaowarat is lively and noisy all night — not for light sleepers
Entry rooms are compact, better for couples than larger families

entries.name: INNSiDE by Meliá Bangkok Sukhumvit
entries.addr: 1472 Sukhumvit Road, Phra Khanong, Khlong Toei, Bangkok
entries.storyHtml: INNSiDE by Meliá is a design hotel from the Spanish Meliá group, right by BTS On Nut — step out and you're at the station, scoring 9.1 from over 1,027 reviews. What reviews praise are the floor-to-ceiling windows with city views, the rooftop pool and bar, and a well-rated breakfast. On Nut is packed with restaurants and night markets, and it's a short BTS ride to Siam or Asoke — ideal if you want good design at a mid-range price right on the skytrain.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: ask for a Corner room — brighter and more open. Head up to the rooftop bar for evening city views, then walk to the On Nut night markets.
pros: Right by BTS On Nut — step out and you're at the station
Modern design hotel, big windows with city views
Rooftop pool and bar with good city views
Well-rated breakfast · plenty of restaurants in On Nut
cons: Entry rooms are a compact 20 sqm, design-hotel style
On Nut is on outer Sukhumvit, further from Siam than inner stops

entries.name: ibis Styles Bangkok Silom
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Silom · near BTS Sala Daeng / MRT Silom
entries.addr: 289 Silom Road, Silom, Bang Rak, Bangkok
entries.storyHtml: ibis Styles Silom is the most-reviewed hotel in this guide — over 2,387 reviews and still a high 9.2, rare consistency at a from-฿1,500 price. The strength is its Silom Road location within walking distance of both BTS Sala Daeng and MRT Silom, so you can pick either line. Bright ibis Styles design, clean rooms and breakfast included — ideal for value in the business district with easy access everywhere.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Silom is a business area by day and lively near Patpong at night. Ask for a Superior room or above for a brighter, fresher room than the Standard.
pros: Most reviewed in this guide, 2,387, with a consistent 9.2
Walk to both BTS Sala Daeng and MRT Silom — two lines
Great-value starting price for a central business-district spot
Bright design, clean rooms, breakfast included
cons: Standard rooms are a compact 18 sqm, built for sleep and transit
Silom is lively at night — there may be some street noise

entries.name: The Salil Hotel Sukhumvit 57 - Thonglor
entries.addr: 24 Soi Sukhumvit 57, Khlong Tan Nuea, Watthana, Bangkok
entries.storyHtml: The Salil is an English-styled boutique hotel in the heart of Thonglor with a strong 1,214 reviews, scoring 8.9. Its strengths are the warm English-house design and rooms larger than average with a mini-kitchen corner. It sits on Soi Sukhumvit 57 near BTS Thong Lo, in Bangkok's hippest cafe, dining and nightlife district — ideal if you want a boutique feel and to live the Thonglor lifestyle.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: from the hotel, walk to the mouth of the soi and grab a motorbike taxi or walk to the BTS. The entry Premier room is already roomy; upgrade to a suite only for longer stays.
pros: Warm, distinctive English-style decor
Rooms larger than average, with a mini-kitchen corner
In Thonglor — hip cafes and restaurants within walking distance
1,214 reviews, praise for the rooms and location
cons: On Soi Sukhumvit 57, a fair walk to BTS Thong Lo
Thonglor food and drink prices run higher than other areas

entries.name: ASAI Bangkok Chinatown
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chinatown·Charoen Krung · near MRT Wat Mangkon
tags: 💰 Good design at a fair price
entries.addr: 531 Charoen Krung Road, Pom Prap Sattru Phai, Bangkok
entries.storyHtml: ASAI Bangkok Chinatown is a design hotel from the ASAI by Dusit brand that delivers good design at a fair price, with a strong 1,473 reviews and a 9.0 score. The rooms are compact but well laid out, with a modern courtyard and communal spaces. It sits on Charoen Krung near MRT Wat Mangkon, a walk into Yaowarat and the street-food lanes — ideal if you want a well-designed room next to Chinatown without paying a premium.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: entry rooms are compact; for quiet, ask for a Courtyard-facing room. Travelling as a small group or family, choose the Biggy King Bunk with its bunk bed.
pros: ASAI by Dusit design brand — genuinely good design
Near MRT Wat Mangkon, walk into Yaowarat and street food
Great value for a design hotel this central
1,473 reviews, modern communal spaces
cons: Entry rooms ~19 sqm, compact — design over space
Chinatown is lively; street-side rooms may catch noise

entries.name: Hotel Royal Bangkok @ Chinatown
entries.storyHtml: Hotel Royal @ Chinatown is a large 290-room hotel on Yaowarat Road with a rooftop pool from just ฿1,400, with a hefty 1,498 reviews and a 9.0 score. The strengths are its location by MRT Wat Mangkon — step out into Yaowarat and the street food — plus a rooftop pool that's rare at this price. Ideal for travellers who want to stay in the heart of Chinatown on a budget while still getting full facilities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: the entry Superior rooms have no window; upgrade to a Deluxe for natural light. Head to the rooftop pool in the evening for Yaowarat views.
pros: A rooftop pool — rare at a from-฿1,400 price
By MRT Wat Mangkon, step out into Yaowarat and street food
Large 290-room hotel with full facilities
1,498 reviews, good value in the heart of Chinatown
cons: Entry Superior rooms have no window; upgrade to Deluxe
A large standard hotel — no boutique charm

entries.name: ibis Bangkok Siam
entries.addr: 927 Rama I Road, Wang Mai, Pathum Wan, Bangkok
entries.storyHtml: ibis Bangkok Siam is an ibis hotel right by BTS National Stadium in the heart of Siam, scoring 8.7 from over 1,113 reviews. The clear selling point is the location — walk to MBK and Siam Square, and hop on the BTS anywhere — from ฿1,500. You get clean, predictable ibis-standard rooms where you know what you'll get. Best for travellers who prioritise shopping and skytrain access on a budget over room atmosphere.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: standard rooms are a compact 17 sqm — ask for a high-floor city-view room for more light and quiet. Easy walk to MBK and Siam Square for shopping.
pros: By BTS National Stadium, walk to MBK and Siam Square
Reliable ibis standard, clean rooms
From ฿1,500 — good value for a central Siam spot
1,113 reviews, praise for location and value
cons: Standard rooms are a small 17 sqm — for sleep and transit
Chain-hotel style, no distinctive character

entries.name: Lub d Bangkok Siam
entries.addr: 925/9 Rama I Road, Wang Mai, Pathum Wan, Bangkok
entries.storyHtml: Lub d Bangkok Siam is the top-scoring option in the budget tier — 9.2 from the recently renovated Lub d brand. The strength is dorms designed better than the usual hostel, with a privacy curtain, reading light, charging socket and locker at every bed, plus social spaces to meet fellow travellers. It's by BTS National Stadium in central Siam, from just ฿650 a bed, and has private rooms for those who'd rather not share.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: solo female travellers may prefer the female-only dorm. For privacy on a smaller budget, The Compact is a private room from ฿1,500.
pros: Top score in the budget tier, 9.2, recently renovated Lub d
Well-designed dorms — curtain, light, socket, locker per bed
By BTS National Stadium in central Siam, easy to get around
Private rooms available for those who don't want a dorm
cons: Dorms are shared — not for those who need full privacy
Limited private rooms, fill up fast in high season

entries.name: Silom Space Hostel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Silom · by BTS Sala Daeng / near MRT Silom
entries.addr: 8 Silom Road, Suriya Wong, Bang Rak, Bangkok
entries.storyHtml: Silom Space Hostel is the cheapest option in this guide — from just ฿300 a bed, yet right on Silom Road. It suits backpackers and budget travellers who prioritise location and price. Real guest reviews note the location by BTS Sala Daeng and near MRT Silom — two lines to choose from — but the 7.5 score reflects that this is a basic, value-focused hostel rather than a designer one. There are both dorms and private rooms depending on your budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: the low price comes with basic facilities — check the latest reviews and room photos before booking. For privacy, choose the Double room from ฿750.
pros: Cheapest in this guide, from ฿300 a bed
On Silom Road, by BTS Sala Daeng / near MRT Silom
Two lines to choose from — easy access to town
Private rooms available for those who don't want a dorm
cons: 7.5, the lowest score here — a basic, value-focused hostel
Limited facilities; check the latest reviews before booking

faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Bangkok hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Bangkok?
faq.a: It depends on your travel style. Siam suits shoppers who want the BTS to anywhere (Siam@Siam, ibis Siam, Lub d). Sukhumvit/Thonglor suits food and nightlife lovers (INNSiDE, The Salil). Silom is the business district on both BTS and MRT (ibis Styles Silom, Silom Space). Chinatown suits street-food fans (Shanghai Mansion, ASAI, Hotel Royal). The Riverside suits a luxury, restful stay (Mandarin Oriental, The Peninsula).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Bangkok hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: hostels from around ฿300–700 a bed; quality 3-star and boutique hotels around ฿1,400–3,200 a night; 4-star around ฿2,500–4,500; riverside 5-star luxury from ฿11,000–16,000+. During festivals (Songkran, New Year, long weekends) prices can run well above normal.

faq.q: ❓ Which Bangkok hotel is easiest for getting around?
faq.a: Pick a hotel on or near the BTS/MRT to avoid the worst traffic — for example Siam@Siam and ibis Siam by BTS National Stadium, INNSiDE by BTS On Nut, ibis Styles Silom near BTS Sala Daeng / MRT Silom, and ASAI and Hotel Royal near MRT Wat Mangkon. The riverside hotels like Mandarin Oriental and The Peninsula run shuttle boats that connect to BTS Saphan Taksin.

faq.q: ❓ How far in advance should I book a Bangkok hotel?
faq.a: For ordinary weekdays, 1–3 weeks ahead is enough since Bangkok has a huge supply of rooms. But around Songkran (13–15 April), New Year, long weekends and major events, the good rooms at good rates fill fast — book a month or more ahead, especially riverside hotels and small boutiques.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest to book a Bangkok hotel?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by the promotions running at the time, so it's worth comparing all 3 before every booking — each review page in this guide has price-comparison links, which can save several hundred baht a night.

faq.q: ❓ How do I get from the airport into Bangkok?
faq.a: From Suvarnabhumi (BKK), take the Airport Rail Link into town and connect to BTS/MRT to skip the traffic, or grab a taxi/Grab. From Don Muang (DMK), use taxi, Grab or bus/van into town. If your hotel is on the Chao Phraya, get off the train and connect to a hotel ferry or express boat.
